title: Runic quantum notation as a symbolic layer
description: A proposed notation layer that assigns runic labels to explicit finite-dimensional quantum-information objects without changing their mathematical or physical content.
confusion_guard: Runic names and images are notation for a proposed state-space model. They are not physical particles, forces, frequencies or quantum operators without explicit matrices, units and measurements.
definitions: A 16-dimensional register has Hilbert-space dimension 16 = 2^4 and can represent four qubits or one 16-level qudit.
A rune label r is a symbolic identifier for a basis state, observable, gate or channel only after its mathematical type is declared.
A valid state is |psi> = sum_j a_j |j> with sum_j |a_j|^2 = 1.
Odin's eye is a symbolic review boundary: open means the label has a defined type and inverse/check; closed means the identity gap remains.
mechanism: The symbolic layer maps runic labels to already defined finite-dimensional quantum-information objects. The underlying state vector, unitary gate, channel or measurement must remain explicit; visual resemblance does not supply the map.
predictions: Every accepted rune-to-object map is type-checkable as a basis label, unitary operator, channel or observable.
Every accepted state preserves normalization and every accepted unitary satisfies U^dagger U = I.
A declared measurement produces probabilities P(j) = |<j|psi>|^2.
Removing the runic labels leaves the same quantum-information calculation.
assumptions: The runic labels are a notation layer and do not add physical degrees of freedom.
The register dimension and subsystem decomposition are declared before computation.
Any proposed operator is represented by an explicit finite matrix or completely positive map.
The digital calculation is a classical simulation unless independently implemented and verified on quantum hardware.
falsification_conditions: Reject a mapping if the same rune is assigned incompatible mathematical types without a declared context.
Reject a gate if it fails the unitary or channel validity conditions.
Reject a state if normalization or Born probabilities fail beyond numerical tolerance.
Do not promote the symbolic layer if it produces no reproducible prediction beyond relabeling an existing model.

evidence.source: Finite-dimensional Hilbert-space and qudit definitions already present in UPI
evidence.notes: Supports the mathematical substrate only; it does not validate the runic interpretation.
Visual and symbolic proposal; not an experimental observation.

stop_reason: No explicit rune-to-operator dictionary, independent physical system or new measurable prediction has been supplied. The smallest next observation is one complete table assigning each rune a type, matrix or channel, units where applicable, and a round-trip test.
